passage.title: The Pirahã people of Brazil
passage.subtitle: The Pirahã language has stirred up debate among experts
paragraphs: The Pirahã tribe live deep in Brazil’s Amazon forest, and their language is hotly debated by linguists. Since 1977, the ethnologist Daniel Everett has spent a total of seven years living with the Pirahã and has committed his career to studying their puzzling speech. Indeed, he has been uncertain for so long about what he was actually hearing while living among the Pirahã that he waited nearly three decades before publishing his findings.

The debate over the Pirahã language goes right to the core of the riddle regarding how Homo sapiens managed to develop vocal communication. Although bees dance, birds sing and whales even sing with syntax, human language is unique, if only for the reason that it enables humans to piece together never-before-constructed thoughts, and be infinitely imaginative - think of Shakespeare’s plays or Einstein’s theory of relativity.

Linguistics generally focuses on what features all human languages have in common, but the Pirahã language departs from what some academics have long maintained are essential and inalienable features of all human languages. Most of all, it may be unique for not employing subordinate clauses. Instead of saying, ’When I have finished eating, I will speak to you,’ the Pirahã say, ’I finish eating, I speak with you.’ Equally perplexing, the Pirahã appear not to use numbers. During the time he spent with them, Everett never heard words like ’all’, ’every’ and ’more’. There is one word, ’hoi’, that comes close to the numeral 1, but it can also mean ’small’. And they were never observed to count without language, on their fingers for example, in order to determine important tasks in village life like how many pieces of meat to grill.

Everett’s findings among the Pirahã have brought new life to a controversial theory by the linguist Benjamin Whorf, who suggested that people are only capable of constructing thoughts for which they possess actual words. Or to put it another way, because they have no words for numbers, they cannot even begin to understand the concept of numbers or arithmetic.

The Warlpiri language - spoken by a group of Australian Aborigines-like that of the Pirahã, features only the most rudimentary system of counting. However, the Warlpiri people had no difficulty counting farther than three in a foreign language, in this case English, but when Everett attempted to teach the Pirahã how to count in Portuguese like other Brazilians, not a single person could count to 10.

Everett is at pains to point out that the Pirahã are not unintelligent, for their thinking is not any slower than that of the average university student. And although they reside in a remote part of the forest, they do not live in complete genetic isolation, but mix with people from the surrounding populations and and share similar intellectual capacities with their neighbours whose languages do contain numbers.

Eventually, after some 30 years of research, Everett has come up with a surprising explanation for the peculiarities of the Pirahã language. Language, he believes, is created by a people’s way of life, their belief system and values. In this way, variety in human language is almost limitless, a function of the human capacity to live in different ways, such as in the forest. What Everett’s research has revealed is that the central tenet of the Pirahã culture is to live in the here and now. The only thing of importance that is worth communicating to others is what is being experienced at that very moment, though this can often be described with great care and detail. In consequence, the language has no means to conjugate verbs in order to describe ’yesterday’ or ’last week’ or ’when I was a child’. Their very literal view of the world curtails abstract thought, and many features taken for granted among other peoples are absent among the Pirahã, such as a creation myth, story telling and painting. One manifestation of their beliefs is that by tradition the names they give their children are not particularly imaginative. Often they are named after other members of the tribe with whom they share similar character traits. Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.

Everett anticipated that these findings would be controversial and the reaction came as expected. Until this point, many linguists had defended the theories of Noam Chomsky, according to which all human languages have a universal grammar. What exactly makes up this universal grammar is the subject of debate, but at its heart is the concept of ’recursion’, which is defined as replication of a structure within its single parts. Without it, humans would not be able to view separate thoughts as subordinate parts of a complex whole. And, most pertinent to Everett’s work, there would not be subordinate clauses, which are responsible for translating the concept of recursion into grammar.

But if the Pirahã do not form subordinate clauses, then recursion cannot explain the uniqueness of human language, and this would negate Chomsky’s theories. The logical way forward now would be to try and prove that the Pirahã can think in a recursive fashion. The only problem is, nobody can confirm or deny Everett’s observations since no other researcher can speak Pirahã as well as he does. Despite this, several researchers - including two of Chomsky’s colleagues - will soon travel to Brazil to check his claims. My concern is that soon the Pirahã will simply become one more scientific oddity with every aspect of their lives being exploited and analysed.

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 1-6 on your answer sheet.

questions.text: What are we told about Daniel Everett in the first paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: He has lived among the Pirahã since 1977.

options.label: B
options.text: It took him seven years to learn the Pirahã language

options.label: C
options.text: No one would publish his research for three decades.

options.label: D
options.text: Studying the Pirahã language is the focus of his work.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Chúng ta được cho biết điều gì về Daniel Everett trong đoạn đầu tiên?

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Daniel Everett ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
Studying the Pirahã language ~ committed his career to studying their puzzling speech
focus of his work ~ committed his career

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "'Từ năm 1977, nhà dân tộc học Daniel Everett đã dành tổng cộng bảy năm sống với người Pirahã và cống hiến sự nghiệp của mình để nghiên cứu thứ tiếng bí ẩn của họ.'". (Since 1977, the ethnologist Daniel Everett has spent a total of seven years living with the Pirahã and has committed his career to studying their puzzling speech.)
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Việc nghiên cứu ngôn ngữ Pirahã là trọng tâm công việc của ông" (Studying the Pirahã language is the focus of his work).

Bước 4: Đáp án: D
quotes: Since 1977, the ethnologist Daniel Everett has spent a total of seven years living with the Pirahã and has committed his career to studying their puzzling speech.

questions.text: Which of the following is the best summary of the second paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: Humans are the only species to be linguistically creative.

options.label: B
options.text: Humans, bees, birds and whales share a characteristic

options.label: C
options.text: Human language is not fully understood by scientists.

options.label: D
options.text: Humans are the only species to use syntax.

quotes: Although bees dance, birds sing and whales even sing with syntax, human language is unique, if only for the reason that it enables humans to piece together never-before-constructed thoughts, and be infinitely imaginative - think of Shakespeare’s plays or Einstein’s theory of relativity.

questions.text: Why does the writer refer to subordinate clauses?

options.label: A
options.text: to criticise the general approach of linguistics

options.label: B
options.text: to compare two features of the Pirahã language

options.label: C
options.text: to explain why the Pirahã language is difficult to learn

options.label: D
options.text: to exemplify an unusual feature of the Pirahã language.

quotes: Most of all, it may be unique for not employing subordinate clauses.

questions.text: What point does the writer make about the work of Whorf?

options.label: A
options.text: He thought that numbers were common to all human languages.

options.label: B
options.text: His theory might be supported by Everett's research.

options.label: C
options.text: His research enabled him to find a new life among the Pirahã.

options.label: D
options.text: He predicted that people like the Pirahã would never be found.

quotes: Everett’s findings among the Pirahã have brought new life to a controversial theory by the linguist Benjamin Whorf, who suggested that people are only capable of constructing thoughts for which they possess actual words.

questions.text: The writer refers to the Warlpiri people in order to

options.label: A
options.text: suggest that the Pirahã be taught to count in English.

options.label: B
options.text: show how tribal peoples learn a foreign language.

options.label: C
options.text: compare counting in English and Portuguese.

options.label: D
options.text: illustrate the uniqueness of the Pirahã.

quotes: The Warlpiri language - spoken by a group of Australian Aborigines-like that of the Pirahã, features only the most rudimentary system of counting. However, the Warlpiri people had no difficulty counting farther than three in a foreign language, in this case English, but when Everett attempted to teach the Pirahã how to count in Portuguese like other Brazilians, not a single person could count to 10.

questions.text: What is Everett's point about the Pirahã's intellectual capacities?

options.label: A
options.text: Pirahã students have not graduated from universities.

options.label: B
options.text: He does not want people to criticise their intelligence.

options.label: C
options.text: Their isolation makes it difficult to evaluate their intelligence.

options.label: D
options.text: He believes their language is more complex than their neighbours'.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Quan điểm của Everett về khả năng trí tuệ của người Pirahã là gì?

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Everett's point ~ Everett is at pains to point out
Pirahã's intellectual capacities ~ Pirahã are not unintelligent
He does not want people to criticise their intelligence ~ Everett is at pains to point out that the Pirahã are not unintelligent

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Everett rất vất vả để chỉ ra rằng người Pirahã không phải là những người kém thông minh, vì cách suy nghĩ của họ không hề chậm hơn so với một sinh viên đại học bình thường." (Everett is at pains to point out that the Pirahã are not unintelligent, for their thinking is not any slower than that of the average university student.)
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Ông không muốn mọi người chỉ trích trí thông minh của họ" (He does not want people to criticise their intelligence).

Bước 4: Đáp án: B
quotes: Everett is at pains to point out that the Pirahã are not unintelligent, for their thinking is not any slower than that of the average university student.

question_groups.body:
Everett's explanation
Everett believes that a group's language is a product of their ____ (7), and thus language is infinitely varied. During the time he spent living among them, he observed that the Pirahã only place value on the ____ (8), and have no ____ (9) to describe completed events. Similarly, the types of names they use reflect the fact that they do not celebrate ____ (10).
question_groups.body_html:
Everett's explanation

Everett believes that a group's language is a product of their [7], and thus language is infinitely varied. During the time he spent living among them, he observed that the Pirahã only place value on the [8], and have no [9] to describe completed events. Similarly, the types of names they use reflect the fact that they do not celebrate [10].

quotes: Language, he believes, is created by a people’s way of life, their belief system and values.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Trong thời gian sống giữa họ, ông quan sát thấy người Pirahã chỉ đặt giá trị vào ___
Vị trí trống cần một danh từ để chỉ thứ mà người Pirahã đặt giá trị.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: place value on the + NOUN (NOUN là đối tượng của sự đặt giá trị)

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Pirahã only place value on the ~ central tenet of the Pirahã culture is to live in the here and now.
observed ~ revealed

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: 'What Everett's research has revealed is that the central tenet of the Pirahã culture is to live in the here and now.'. "Here and now" đồng nghĩa với present (hiện tại).

Bước 5: Đáp án: A
Người Pirahã chỉ đặt giá trị vào hiện tại (the Pirahã only place value on the present).
quotes: What Everett’s research has revealed is that the central tenet of the Pirahã culture is to live in the here and now.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
và không có ___ nào để mô tả các sự kiện đã hoàn thành.
Vị trí trống cần một danh từ số nhiều để chỉ một phương tiện hoặc cách thức.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN (số nhiều)
Dấu hiệu: have no + NOUN + to describe (NOUN là thứ thiếu để mô tả)

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
no ... to describe completed events ~ language has no means to conjugate verbs in order to describe 'yesterday' or 'last week' or 'when I was a child'

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "In consequence, the language has no means to conjugate verbs in order to describe 'yesterday' or 'last week' or 'when I was a child.". "Means to conjugate verbs" liên quan đến grammar (ngữ pháp).

Bước 5: Đáp án: F
và không có ngữ pháp nào để mô tả các sự kiện đã hoàn thành (and have no grammar to describe completed events).
quotes: In consequence, the language has no means to conjugate verbs in order to describe ’yesterday’ or ’last week’ or ’when I was a child’.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Tương tự, các loại tên mà họ sử dụng phản ánh sự thật rằng họ không tôn vinh ___
Vị trí trống cần một danh từ để chỉ điều mà họ không tôn vinh.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: do not celebrate + NOUN (NOUN là đối tượng của việc không tôn vinh)

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
types of names they use reflect the fact that they do not celebrate ~ Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: 'Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.'. Việc không khuyến khích "standing out or being different" đồng nghĩa với việc không tôn vinh individuality (cá tính).

Bước 5: Đáp án: H
họ không tôn vinh cá tính (they do not celebrate individuality).
quotes: Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.

questions.text: Everett was surprised by the way his research was greeted
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Everett đã ngạc nhiên về cách nghiên cứu của mình được đón nhận.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Everett ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
how his research was greeted ~ the reaction came as expected

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Everett đã dự đoán rằng những phát hiện này sẽ gây tranh cãi và phản ứng đã đến đúng như mong đợi". (Everett anticipated that these findings would be controversial and the reaction came as expected.)
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Everett đã ngạc nhiên" (Everett was surprised). Bài đọc nói rằng phản ứng "đến như dự kiến", không phải là ngạc nhiên.

Bước 4: Đáp án: NO
quotes: Everett anticipated that these findings would be controversial and the reaction came as expected.

questions.text: Chomsky has been critical of Everett's research methodology
quotes: Despite this, several researchers - including two of Chomsky’s colleagues - will soon travel to Brazil to check his claims.

questions.text: If 'recursion' as a universal concept is disproved, Chomsky's ideas about language would be wrong
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Nếu 'recursion' (đệ quy) như một khái niệm phổ quát bị bác bỏ, các ý tưởng của Chomsky về ngôn ngữ sẽ sai.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
'recursion' as a universal concept is disproved ~ then recursion cannot explain the uniqueness of human language
Chomsky's ideas about language would be wrong ~ negate Chomsky's theories

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Nhưng nếu người Pirahã không hình thành các mệnh đề phụ, thì đệ quy không thể giải thích tính độc đáo của ngôn ngữ loài người, và điều này sẽ phủ nhận các lý thuyết của Chomsky." (But if the Pirahã do not form subordinate clauses, then recursion cannot explain the uniqueness of human language, and this would negate Chomsky's theories.)
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "các ý tưởng của Chomsky về ngôn ngữ sẽ sai" (Chomsky's ideas about language would be wrong).

Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: But if the Pirahã do not form subordinate clauses, then recursion cannot explain the uniqueness of human language, and this would negate Chomsky’s theories.

questions.text: The Pirahã will benefit from their new-found status among academics
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Người Pirahã sẽ hưởng lợi từ địa vị mới của họ trong giới học thuật.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Pirahã will benefit ~ Pirahã will simply become one more scientific oddity with every aspect of their lives being exploited and analysed.
new-found status among academics ~ scientific oddity, exploited and analysed

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "'Mối lo ngại của tôi là chẳng bao lâu nữa người Pirahã sẽ chỉ đơn thuần trở thành một hiện tượng khoa học kỳ lạ nữa, với mọi khía cạnh trong cuộc sống của họ bị khai thác và phân tích'". (My concern is that soon the Pirahã will simply become one more scientific oddity with every aspect of their lives being exploited and analysed.)
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Người Pirahã sẽ hưởng lợi" (The Pirahã will benefit). Người viết bày tỏ lo ngại về việc họ sẽ bị "khai thác và phân tích" chứ không phải hưởng lợi.

Bước 4: Đáp án: NO
quotes: My concern is that soon the Pirahã will simply become one more scientific oddity with every aspect of their lives being exploited and analysed.
